transcript: If you are going to overthink, then overthink the positives. Overthink the best outcome. Overthink how good this life could be. Overthink how peaceful it would feel if things slowly, quietly worked out. Because the mind has a habit, it leans toward fear. It replays the past. It worries about a future that hasn't arrived. We imagine the worst case scenario. We revisit old mistakes. We carry tomorrow's weight before it is real. But what if the mind is gently turned in another direction? Let this be the intention for 2026. To overthink the positives, even if it feels unfamiliar, even if the mind resists at first, some will say it isn't possible. But healing often begins with a new direction of attention. To imagine the best outcome in each moment. To picture the best version of the path unfolding. Friendships that nourish. Places that feel like home. Work that aligns with the spirit. Not by denying what is hard, but by choosing where the mind rests. This may not make life perfect, but it can make it softer, and perhaps a little happier. When a negative thought appears, notice it, thank it, and let it pass. Then gently return attention to what could go right. This is not a rule. It is simply an invitation. If you choose to overthink the positives in 2026, write, I choose peace below, and follow to continue this journey.
